sources.cite: RCW 26.44.030 (last amended 2025 c 197 s 2 and 2025 c 192 s 2): mandated reporters include social service counselors and psychologists; a report is made 'at the first opportunity, but in no case longer than 48 hours' after there is reasonable cause to believe a child has suffered abuse or neglect, to the proper law enforcement agency or to the department
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 through a summary of the statute's page.

sources.cite: RCW 26.44.020 (last amended 2025 c 197 s 1): 'social service counselor' is anyone engaged in a professional capacity in promoting children's health, welfare, support or education, or providing social services to adults or families, including mental health, drug and alcohol and domestic violence programs; abuse or neglect includes injury of a child by any person that harms the child's health, welfare or safety, other than conduct permitted by RCW 9A.16.100
sources.note: Read 2026-11-14 through a summary. RCW 9A.16.100 (physical discipline) could not be opened; this case does not rely on its text.

sources.cite: RCW 26.44.060: a person participating in good faith in a report is immune from civil or criminal liability; RCW 26.44.080: a mandated reporter who knowingly fails to report 'shall be guilty of a gross misdemeanor'
sources.note: Both sections read 2026-11-14 through a summary.

sources.cite: NASW Code of Ethics (approved 1996, revised 2021): 1.01 legal obligations may supersede loyalty to clients; 1.07(c) confidentiality and its limits, the least information necessary; 1.07(d) tell clients about a disclosure and its consequences before disclosing, when feasible, including disclosures required by law; 1.07(e) discuss the limits of confidentiality

brief.situation: You are a licensed social worker at a family resource center in Washington, where you see parents for parenting support. Tasha Greene, 29 (a fictional client), has come for six weeks; her son Malik, 6, stays in the center's childcare during her sessions. Before today's session the childcare aide tells you what she saw and heard (in the notes). Tasha is in your office now; Malik is in the playroom. You have 50 minutes.
handover: Parenting support: Tasha asked for help with Malik's tantrums; she lives with Malik and her boyfriend, Darnell; she works nights at a grocery store.
howItWorks: Choose what to say and do from the action groups. Tasha answers at once; then let the conversation continue, which moves the session clock by the minutes that exchange took.
Her rapport, distress and how much she discloses change with what you say. What she tells you depends on the trust you have built.
The hour ends at 50 minutes. After the session you write a short formulation, make the report if you have not, and document.

source.cite: Common outpatient practice: a 50-minute session (the 'therapy hour')
source.note: Author's scenario timing; the session can be ended earlier.
How rapport and distress move with each response is a teaching simplification for exam practice, not a validated model of a client.

checkIn.label: Open-ended check-in: 'How has the week been?'

effects.log: You ask an open question and give her room.

effects.finding: "Tired. Malik's been mouthy, Darnell's been on him about it. Same old."

reflect.label: Reflect what you hear (empathic reflection)
reflect.why: You have reflected a lot already; move the session on.

effects.log: You reflect the feeling under what was said, without judging it.

effects.finding: Tasha nods slowly. "Yeah. I'm just tired of everybody yelling."

askHome.label: Ask openly how discipline goes at home these days

effects.log: You ask, without leading, how discipline goes at home.

then.finding: She looks at her hands. "Darnell whoops him when he talks back. With a belt, or the phone cord. I hate it. I told him to stop."

then.log: Her account fits what the aide saw.

then.finding: "Normal stuff. Time-outs." (She is not ready to tell you more.)

askSafety.label: Ask whether Malik and she are safe tonight: is Darnell at home, has he hurt her

effects.log: You ask who is at home tonight and whether Darnell has hurt her.

effects.finding: "He's there. He's never hit me. My sister's place is always open."

questionChild.label: Go to the childcare room and question Malik about the marks in detail

effects.log: You leave Tasha and question Malik about how he was hurt.

effects.finding: Malik cries and says he doesn't want to talk. Tasha is in the doorway: "What are you doing with my son?"

effects.log: Investigating is child protective services' job; repeated questioning can distress a child and muddy the investigation. Reasonable cause is enough to report.

tellDuty.label: Tell her honestly: you are required to report what was seen and said today, what happens next, and that you will stay with her through it

effects.log: You tell Tasha plainly that you must report what the aide saw and what she told you, what an intake call involves, and that you will keep working with her.

then.finding: She cries. "They're going to take him." Then: "Okay. I want Darnell gone anyway. I just didn't know how."

askPermission.label: Ask her whether she wants you to make a report
askPermission.available: not talking and (not askedPermission and not reported)

effects.log: You ask Tasha whether she wants you to report.
A mandated report is not hers to permit or refuse (RCW 26.44.030).

promise.label: Promise her nothing will happen to her family

effects.log: You promise her nothing will happen to the family.
A promise you cannot keep: what follows a report is not yours to decide.

callNow.label: Call the child abuse intake line now, from your office, with her there

effects.log: You call the state's child abuse intake line and report what the aide saw, what Malik and Tasha said, that Darnell is at the home tonight, and the sister's address.

effects.finding: Intake takes the report and asks where Malik will sleep tonight. Tasha listens, holding his jacket.

effects.log: Reported at the first opportunity (RCW 26.44.030).

safetyPlan.label: Plan tonight with her: where she and Malik will sleep, and what she will say if Darnell calls
safetyPlan.available: not talking and (safetyAsked and not safePlan)
safetyPlan.why: Ask who is at home first (or it is planned).

effects.log: You plan tonight with her.

then.finding: She will take Malik to her sister's straight from here; she won't argue with Darnell by phone; she will call the hotline if he shows up.

callDarnell.label: Call Darnell and tell him to stop hitting the boy

effects.log: You call Darnell and tell him what you know.

effects.finding: He hangs up. Tasha goes pale: "He'll know it was me."

effects.log: Confronting the alleged abuser can put the child and the mother at greater risk and tip him off before the investigation.

keepEngaged.label: Offer to keep working with her: parenting support, help with a protection order if she wants one, and a session this week

effects.log: You offer to keep going: parenting support, help with a protection order if she chooses, and a session this week.

options.label: Call intake now, before you leave today
Wait until next week's session to learn more first
Leave it to Tasha; she said she will handle it

then.log: Reported after the session, the same day.

document.label: Document
document.why: Decide about the report first (or it is documented).

options.label: What the aide saw and Malik said, in their words; what Tasha said; the report: when, to whom, the reference number; the safety plan for tonight; your next contact
'Mother's boyfriend is abusing the child; mother failed to protect'

effects.log: Documented: {record}.
You close the session.

effects.log: The 50-minute hour is up. The session ends here.
The client stands, says this is not helping, and leaves before the hour is over.

enough.title: Predict (not scored)
enough.context: You have the aide's account: looped bruises and 'Darnell used the cord.' Is that enough to report, or do you need Tasha to confirm it first?

choices.label: Enough: reasonable cause, not proof, is the standard

effects.log: Prediction: report on reasonable cause.

choices.feedback: Right. RCW 26.44.030 runs from 'reasonable cause to believe' a child has suffered abuse or neglect, and the report is due at the first opportunity. Confirming is the investigators' job, not yours.

choices.label: Get her account first, then decide

effects.log: Prediction: confirm first.

choices.feedback: Not needed. Her account helps you plan with her, but the duty already runs from reasonable cause (RCW 26.44.030). You do not investigate or wait for proof.

formulation.question: Write your formulation: why you reported, when, and how you kept Tasha engaged while you did.

parts.label: The duty
parts.criteria: Reasonable cause from the aide's observation and Malik's words; as a social service counselor you report at the first opportunity and within 48 hours (RCW 26.44.030); you report, you do not investigate or seek permission; good-faith reports are immune (RCW 26.44.060).
parts.modelAnswer: Looped bruises on a six-year-old's thighs and his words 'Darnell used the cord' are reasonable cause to believe he has been abused. At a family resource center I am a social service counselor and a mandated reporter (RCW 26.44.020, .030), so I reported to intake at the first opportunity, today. Confirming what happened is the investigators' job; I did not question Malik or ask Tasha's permission.

parts.label: Keeping the family engaged
parts.criteria: Told her honestly before calling and why (NASW 1.07(d)); no promises about the outcome; planned tonight's safety with her; offered continued support; did not confront Darnell; documented facts, not conclusions.
parts.modelAnswer: I told Tasha first what I had to do, why, and what an intake call involves, without promising an outcome (NASW 1.07(d)). We planned tonight: she and Malik go to her sister's. I offered to keep working with her, including help with a protection order if she chooses, and a session Thursday. I documented what was seen and said, in their words, and the report details.

source.note: Rapport at the close of the session.
Not used by this case's endings: the report is judged by whether it was made in the session, after it, or not today (RCW 26.44.030's 'first opportunity').

expertPath.text: Check in and reflect; ask openly how discipline goes at home, and who is home tonight.
Tell her honestly that you must report, why, and what happens next; no promises.
Call intake with her there; plan tonight at her sister's.
Offer to keep working with her (parenting support, help with a protection order if she wants it, Thursday); document facts after.

reportedEngaged.headline: Good: reported, and still working together
reportedEngaged.body: You reported on reasonable cause at the first opportunity, told her first, did not investigate, and planned tonight's safety with her.

gaps.headline: Reported, with gaps
gaps.body: The report is made; the criteria below show what was late or missing.

reportedLost.headline: Reported, at the cost of the relationship
reportedLost.body: NASW 1.07(d) asks you to tell her before you disclose, when feasible. Honesty about the report, without promises, is what keeps a parent coming back.

confrontedEnd.headline: Tipped off
confrontedEnd.body: Confronting the alleged abuser can endanger the child and the parent and get ahead of the investigation. Report, plan safety, and let child protective services act.

notReported.headline: No report
notReported.body: Reasonable cause, not proof, starts the duty; the report is due at the first opportunity and within 48 hours (RCW 26.44.030), and it is not the parent's to make for you. A mandated reporter who knowingly fails to report commits a gross misdemeanor (RCW 26.44.080).

walkout.headline: She left
walkout.body: A parent who feels accused leaves with the child. Calm, honest, nonjudgmental talk keeps her in the room long enough to plan.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: Nothing was documented before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: The aide's observation and Malik's words are reasonable cause; as a social service counselor you are a mandated reporter, and the report is due at the first opportunity (RCW 26.44.030). You report; you do not question the child, seek the parent's permission or confront the boyfriend. Tell Tasha first and honestly, without promises (NASW 1.07(d)); call intake with her there; plan where she and Malik sleep tonight; and offer to keep working with her. Document what was seen and said, not conclusions.
